questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant, so the three significant figures are 4, 6 and 2. The next digit is 8, which is 5 or more, so the 2 rounds up to 3, giving $0.00463$.

distractorRationale.a: Rounded to 3 decimal places instead of 3 significant figures
distractorRationale.b: Truncated after the third significant figure instead of rounding

questions.explanation: The first two significant figures are 3 and 4. The next digit is 5, so the 4 rounds up to 5. The remaining places are filled with zeros to preserve the size, giving $3500$.

distractorRationale.a: Kept only two digits and dropped the place value, changing the size by a factor of 100
distractorRationale.b: Truncated instead of rounding up when the next digit was 5

questions.explanation: Two decimal places means keeping the digits 3 and 8. The next digit is 5, so the 8 rounds up to 9, giving $24.39$.

distractorRationale.a: Truncated rather than rounding, ignoring the 5 that follows
distractorRationale.c: Rounded twice — first to 24.4 at one decimal place, then padded with a zero

questions.explanation: The decimal point must move 5 places to the right to turn $0.0000453$ into $4.53$. Moving right means a negative power, so the answer is $4.53 \times 10^{-5}$.

distractorRationale.a: Counted the zeros after the point but forgot the place occupied by the 4 itself
distractorRationale.c: Correct digits but a positive power, which would give a number in the hundreds of thousands
distractorRationale.d: Numerically equal but not in standard form, since 45.3 is not between 1 and 10

questions.explanation: Writing $8\,750\,000$ as $8.75$ requires moving the decimal point 6 places to the left, so the power of ten is 6. Check: $8.75 \times 1\,000\,000 = 8\,750\,000$.

distractorRationale.a: Counted one place too few; this value is 875,000
distractorRationale.c: Counted the digits rather than the places moved; this value is 87,500,000
distractorRationale.d: Numerically equal but 87.5 is not between 1 and 10, so it is not standard form

questions.stem: Evaluate $(3 \times 10^{5}) \times (4 \times 10^{-2})$, leaving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: Multiply the number parts: $3 \times 4 = 12$. Add the indices: $5 + (-2) = 3$, giving $12 \times 10^{3}$. Since 12 is not between 1 and 10, rewrite it as $1.2 \times 10^{1}$, so the answer is $1.2 \times 10^{4}$.

distractorRationale.a: Stopped at $12 \times 10^3$ and rewrote 12 as 1.2 without adjusting the power
distractorRationale.c: Added the number parts instead of multiplying them
distractorRationale.d: Multiplied the indices instead of adding them

questions.stem: A student measured a length as 4.8 cm when the true length was 5.0 cm. Calculate the percentage error. Give the number only.
questions.explanation: The error is $|4.8 - 5.0| = 0.2$ cm. Percentage error compares this with the true value: $\frac{0.2}{5.0} \times 100\% = 4\%$. Dividing by the measured value instead would wrongly give about 4.17%.
The first three significant figures are 2, 4 and 6. The next digit is 8, so the 6 rounds up to 7, giving $0.247$. Here the leading zero is not counted because it is before the first non-zero digit.

distractorRationale.d: Counted the leading zero as a significant figure, so rounded one place too early

questions.stem: Simplify $\frac{6.4 \times 10^{-3}}{1.6 \times 10^{2}}$, leaving your answer in standard form.
questions.explanation: Divide the number parts: $6.4 \div 1.6 = 4$. Subtract the indices: $-3 - 2 = -5$. So the answer is $4 \times 10^{-5}$.

distractorRationale.a: Subtracted the indices as $-3 - 3$, misreading the denominator index
distractorRationale.c: Added the indices instead of subtracting
distractorRationale.d: Subtracted the top index from the bottom index, reversing the order

questions.stem: A rectangle measures 8.4 cm by 5.2 cm, each length correct to 1 decimal place. Find the maximum possible area of the rectangle, in cm², correct to 2 decimal places.
questions.explanation: A length given to 1 decimal place has an upper bound half a unit above it, so the sides are at most 8.45 cm and 5.25 cm. The maximum area is $8.45 \times 5.25 = 44.3625$, which is $44.36$ cm² to 2 decimal places.

distractorRationale.a: Used the lower bounds 8.35 and 5.15, giving the minimum area instead of the maximum
distractorRationale.b: Multiplied the stated values 8.4 and 5.2, which gives the nominal, not maximum, area
distractorRationale.d: Used 8.5 and 5.3, rounding the bounds up by a whole 0.1 instead of 0.05
